title: Resource Levelling
summary: Resource levelling in plain words: a clash, the quick sum and why it helps, the routine, what to do when a try leaves another clash, exam technique, quick-sum practice and an exit ticket. Most practice is on the Critical Path generator.

els.text: Finishing a project when there are not enough workers

slides.title: The problem

els.text: Each activity needs 1 worker and starts as early as it can.
Between day 12 and day 16, E, F and G all run together. That needs 3 workers, but we only have 2.

slides.brief: Worked example: eight activities, one worker each, only 2 workers available. The project takes 23 days with no limit. Click: the clash.

slides.title: The quick sum

els.text: To fix a clash we hold one activity back. We could draw every choice, but that takes ages.
A quick sum is a fast estimate for each choice: the soonest the whole project could possibly finish if we hold that activity back.
The project might finish later than the quick sum, but never sooner. So the smallest quick sum is the best one to try first.

slides.brief: The one idea. Plain words: a fast estimate, a floor, so we can pick the best option without drawing every one.

slides.title: Working out quick sums

els.text:
The project takes 23 days with no limit. Each activity has a deadline: the latest it can finish without making the project longer.
Quick sum = 23 + the days it finishes past its deadline.
G is held back until F finishes on day 16. It takes 8 days, so it finishes on day 24. Its deadline is day 23, so it is 1 day past: 23 + 1 = 24.

slides.brief: Self-contained: the project time with no limit, each held activity's restart and length, and its deadline are all on the slide. Pupils fill the last three columns, then show the answers. Example: G is held until F finishes at day 16.

slides.title: Try the smallest

els.text: Quick sums: G 24, E 27, F 29. Hold G back until day 16.
G now runs from day 16 to day 24.
No clash is left: never more than 2 workers.
The project takes 24 days. That is the minimum.

slides.brief: Self-contained: the options and their quick sums are repeated, then G is held back to day 16 and the histogram is redrawn.

slides.title: The routine

els.text: Draw the histogram with every activity starting as early as it can. Mark the limit.
Find the first clash. Work out a quick sum for each choice.
Try the smallest quick sum: hold that activity back and redraw.
No clash left? That is the minimum time. Stop.
Still a clash? Work out quick sums for the new clash, add them to the list, and try the smallest on the whole list.

slides.brief: The routine on one slide. Each step appears on a click. Practise it on the generator.

slides.title: When a try leaves another clash

els.text: When a try leaves another clash
The project takes 21 days with no limit.

First clash. Quick sums: C 22, D 26, E 26.
Try C, the smallest.
Holding C back causes a new clash. Quick sums there: F 23, G 22, H 29.
Add them to the same list and try the smallest on the whole list: G, 22.
No clash left. The minimum is 22 days.

slides.brief: Self-contained example with numbers only. Project time with no limit 21; first clash quick sums C 22, D 26, E 26; trying C leaves a new clash with F 23, G 22, H 29; G is smallest on the whole list, and trying G leaves no clash.

slides.title: In the exam

els.text: Look first. Do some activities need so many workers that they can never run together? Add those up.
Use the routine and quick sums.
Stuck? Draw a histogram that fits the limit anyway. It scores 2 of the 3 marks even if it is not the best.

slides.brief: Exam technique: look first, then the routine, then draw it (2 of 3 marks).

slides.title: Quick sums

items.title: Work out the quick sum
question: With no limit the project takes $20$ days.
An activity would finish on day $16$. Its deadline is day $14$.
Work out the quick sum.
items.rationale: Quick sum is the no-limit time plus the days past the deadline.
explanation: It is $2$ days past its deadline.

items.title: Work out the quick sum
question: With no limit the project takes $25$ days.
An activity would finish on day $13$. Its deadline is day $12$.
Work out the quick sum.
items.rationale: Quick sum is the no-limit time plus the days past the deadline.
explanation: It is $1$ day past its deadline.

items.title: Finishes by its deadline
question: With no limit the project takes $18$ days.
An activity would finish on day $15$. Its deadline is day $15$.
Work out the quick sum.
items.rationale: If the activity finishes by its deadline there are no extra days.
explanation: It is not past its deadline, so there are no extra days.

items.title: Finishes before its deadline
question: With no limit the project takes $30$ days.
An activity would finish on day $20$. Its deadline is day $22$.
Work out the quick sum.
items.rationale: If the activity finishes by its deadline there are no extra days.
explanation: It finishes before its deadline, so there are no extra days.

items.title: Which one first?
answer: A $28$, B $27$, C $26$. Try C first.
question: With no limit the project takes $24$ days.
A would finish on day $14$, deadline day $10$.
B would finish on day $15$, deadline day $12$.
C would finish on day $11$, deadline day $9$.
Find each quick sum. Which do you try first?
items.rationale: Try the smallest quick sum first.
explanation: C is the smallest, so try C first.

slides.brief: Five quick-sum questions in plain words. No pictures: the point is the calculation.

slides.title: Exit ticket

els.text: Work on your own. Show your working.

items.title: Work out the quick sum
question: With no limit the project takes $27$ days.
An activity would finish on day $31$. Its deadline is day $24$.
Work out the quick sum.
items.rationale: Quick sum is the no-limit time plus the days past the deadline.
explanation: It is $7$ days past its deadline.

items.title: Which one first?
question: Three choices have quick sums $30$, $28$ and $33$.
Which do you try first?
items.rationale: Try the smallest quick sum first.
explanation: Try the smallest quick sum first: $28$.

items.title: Can it be 30?
answer: No. Even the best choice cannot finish sooner than $31$.
question: The smallest quick sum is $31$.
Can the project finish in $30$ days? Explain.
items.rationale: A quick sum is a floor.
explanation: A quick sum is a floor: the project cannot finish sooner than it.

slides.brief: Last 5 minutes. Question 1 checks the calculation, 2 the order, 3 the floor idea.
